decision_conditions: Prior to the occupation of the development, full details of hard and soft landscaping shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. All hard and soft landscaping and tree planting shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and to a reasonable standard in accordance with the relevant recommendations of appropriate British Standards (in particular, BS 3882:  Specifications for Topsoil, Recommendations (2015) and BS 8545:  Trees from Nursery to Independence in the Landscape, Recommendations (2014) or other recognised codes of good practice). The works shall be carried out prior to the occupation of any part or relevant phase of the development or in accordance with the timetable agreed with the Local Planning Authority. Any tree(s) or plants that (within a period of five years after planting) are removed, die, or (in the opinion of the Local Planning Authority) are damaged or defective shall be replaced as soon as is reasonably practicable with others of a similar size/species/number as originally approved, unless the Local Planning Authority gives its consent to any variation. Reason: To ensure the provision, establishment and maintenance of a reasonable standard of landscape in accordance with the approved designs in accordance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Before any external facing materials are erected or installed on site, external facing materials including windows treatments and finishes shall submitted for the formal written approval of the local planning authority. The development must then be carried out and maintained in accordance with the approved details. Reason: To ensure that the new buildings make a positive contribution to the streetscene and complement the retained buildings on the site, in compliance with Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

All trees shown to be retained shall be subject to protective measures that meet the British Standard BS5837: Trees. The protective measures shall be put in place prior to the permission being implemented (including demolition and site enabling works) and only be removed on completion of the development.  Reason: To ensure retained trees and their root protection areas will not be damaged during demolition or construction in accordance with best practice and Policy 28 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Full details of the secure cycle storage facilities shall be submitted to, and approved in writing by, the Local Planning Authority  showing their positioning within the site, the size and materials of the enclosure and the means of access. The approved details shall be implemented on site prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved and thereafter permanently retained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To ensure the development provides an adequate level of cycle parking facilities and to encourage sustainable modes of transport, in accordance with Policies 36 and 37 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the measures set out in the approved Construction Logistics Plan dated 23 January 2024 (rev 02) produced by REDS10.Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not interfere with the free flow of traffic and conditions of safety on the public highway, and to ensure the development process does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties in accordance with Policies 29 and 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018. This condition is required to be pre-commencement as the Construction Logistics Plan needs to be in place before any works take place and to mitigate against the impacts of the demolition / construction process.

The rating level of any noise emitted from fixed plant and equipment permitted as part of this development shall not exceed L Ar,1hour 38dB during the day. The noise levels shall be measured or calculated 1m externally to any window at the nearest residential facade. Measurements and assessments shall be made according to British Standard BS4142:2014.Reason: To prevent harm to the amenity of neighbouring residents by way of excessive noise, in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The site and building works required to implement the development shall be only carried out between the hours of 08.00 and 18.00 Mondays to Fridays and between 08.00 and 13.00 on Saturdays and not at all on Bank Holidays and Sundays.Reason: To prevent harm to the amenity of neighbouring residents by way of noise and vibration, in accordance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

If, during the course of development, any contamination is found which has not been previously identified, work shall be suspended and additional measures for its remediation shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The remediation of the site shall incorporate the approved additional measures and a verification report for all the remediation works shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.Reason: To prevent harm to human health and pollution of the environment in accordance with the aims and objectives of Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the approved Dust Management Plan (ref: Angel Hill SEND (2144) Version 1.0 - dated 28 September 2023).Reason: To ensure that the proposed development does not have a significant adverse impact on the amenities of nearby residential properties and to minimise the impacts on local air quality in accordance with Policies 29 and 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance "Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition" dated July 2014 (SPG), or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not, without the prior written consent of the local planning authority. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/Reason: To ensure that the development would not result in a deterioration of air quality. This condition is required to be pre-commencement to mitigate against the impacts of the demolition / construction process.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the provisions of the Planning Fire Safety Strategy prepared by Jensen Hughes dated 21 July 2023 (ref: HB/1245/R1 Issue 2)Reason: To ensure that the development incorporates the necessary fire safety measures in accordance with the Mayor's London Plan Policy D12.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Statement & Low and Zero Carbon (LZC) Feasibility Study (Ref: FS0523-MET-ZZ-XX-RP-V-9711) prepared by Method Consulting Ltd and dated 17 July 2023 together with the 'be lean' Technical Note dated 18 July 2023. Prior to first occupation of the new school buildings, 'as-built' BRUKL outputs must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to demonstrate that the development has achieved the targeted reduction in CO2 emissions. If the development is unable to meet the required reduction in CO2 emissions through the approved energy strategy, then any shortfall shall be made up through the application of further sustainability measures. All of the approved measures must thereafter be retained for as long as the development is in existence.Reason: To comply with Policy 31 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the Part L & Overheating Strategy (PO1) prepared by Method Consulting Ltd and dated 6 July 2023. Prior to first occupation, documentary evidence including finalised dynamic thermal modelling results for each of the classrooms and other occupied rooms must submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing which demonstrates that the proposed cooling measures have been implemented and that the relevant TM52 criteria have been achieved in line with the approved overheating strategy.Reason: To comply with Local Plan Policy 33 and London Plan Policy SI 4

Prior to the commencement of development (excluding demolition and enabling works), documentary evidence must be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that the development will achieve an increase in overall green space coverage of at least 10% and an improved Green Space Factor (GSF) score of at least +0.2 compared to the baseline GSF score prior to redevelopment. The council's GSF scoring system set out in the council's 'Technical Guidance Note - Building a Sustainable Sutton' (June 2018) must be used for this purpose. The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.Reason: To comply with Policy 33 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018

The development shall be carried out in accordance with the submitted flood risk assessment (FRA) (ref: REDS10 11446; date: 20 June 2023; rev: P02) and the following mitigation measures it details:o No changes of existing levels within Flood Zones 2 and 3 will be made, as per section 6.14.1 (page 17) of the above-mentioned document.Reason: To prevent flooding elsewhere by ensuring that flood storage will not decrease, in accordance with Policy 32 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and paragraph 165 of the NPPF.

The development hereby approved shall be constructed in accordance with the details stipulated within the approved Preliminary Ecology Appraisal, Bat Surveys and Biodiversity Net Gain Assessment, and thereafter retained.Reason: To enhance and protect the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby permitted, a scheme for wildlife and nesting features shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. These will include:a) Hedgehog holes to increase site connectivity;b) Deadwood log piles and bare sand piles on the biosolar roof to provide nesting habitat for invertebrates; andc) Features on buildings, in accord with the adopted Biodiversity Strategy for a major development, including at least:i) 6 multi-chamber swift bricks (preferred) or boxes;ii) 6 starling boxes;iii) 6 house sparrow terraces;iv) 6 bat bricks (preferred) or boxesd) other bird boxes or features, as appropriate to the site (including insect boxes / solitary bee brick etc.)The scheme will include full details on: numbers of each feature, type of feature / box / brick, location (plan and elevation views) of each feature, height above ground (if applicable) and nearest external lighting (if likely to have an impact).Features shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved scheme and thereafter retained in perpetuity.Reason: To enhance the biodiversity value of the land in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

Prior to first occupation of the development (excluding demolition and site clearance works), an exterior lighting scheme shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The lighting scheme must include:a) Comparison of pre and post-development light, including ambient lighting from the surrounds, presented as 1m centre spot values down to 0.1lux, with isolux contour lines showing light degradation;b) Assessment of external lighting and light spill on existing and proposed habitats;c) the technical details of the luminaires and columns to be used, including their location, type, shape, dimensions and expected luminance output and specifically explaining what design attributes have been chosen to minimise light pollution;f) Consideration of horizontal spill up to 20m from any light fitting that faces habitat along the western, southern and eastern boundaries of the site.f) Vertical spill shown in cross-sectional views.Lighting must be designed to minimise impacts on biodiversity as outlined in Guidance Note 08/18 Bats and Artificial Lighting in the UK (Bats and the Built Environment series by the Institute of Lighting Professionals and the Bat Conservation Trust).Reason: To protect the biodiversity value of the land and adjacent land, in accordance with Policy 26 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development must be carried out in accordance with the approved Air Quality Assessment prepared by Delta-Simons (Project No: 92758.563504)Reason: To ensure that the development meets its Air Quality Neutral aims, protecting and improving local air quality, in compliance with Policy 34 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018 and Policy SI 1 of the London Plan 2021.

The existing vehicle and pedestrian access to Sutton Sports Village from Rose Hill must not be used at any time for the purpose of demolition and construction works associated with the approved development, including the use of existing vehicle parking spaces in the northern section of the site by employees associated with contractors carrying out construction works.Reason: To ensure the continued safe and efficient operation of other facilities and uses within the site during the construction phase, in accordance with Policy 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

No works on implementing the planning permission may be carried out until details have been submitted to and approved by the Council for a scheme of works to widen the main construction vehicle access from Angel Hill. The approved works must then be carried out before any demolition and site clearance works begin on the remainder of the site within the red line of the location plan approved under Condition 1 of this permission. Reason: To minimise impacts on the highway network during the construction and operational phases of the development, in accordance with Policy 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018. The condition is required to be pre-commencement because the demolition and construction impacts of the development cannot be mitigated using a later trigger point.

Details must be submitted to and approved by the Council for a scheme of works to widen the main vehicle access from Rose Hill. The approved works must then be carried out and completed prior to the first occupation of the school. Reason: To minimise impacts on the highway network during the operational phase of the development, in accordance with Policy 36 of the Sutton Local Plan 2018.

The development hereby permitted shall incorporate security measures to minimise the risk of crime and to meet the specific security needs of the development in accordance with the principles and objectives of Secured by Design. Details of these measures, including a certificate of compliance, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority prior to the occupation of the development. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details and retained thereafter. Reason: In order to achieve the principles and objectives of Secured by Design to improve community safety and crime prevention.

Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), a final detailed drainage design, including drawings, supporting calculations, Drainage Assessment Form and SuDS Statement, stating what mitigation measures are being proposed in the event of a pump failure shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. A revised detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks, frequency and who shall be responsible for the maintenance of all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. The system shall be implemented and thereafter managed and maintained in accordance with the approved details.Reason: To prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site in accordance with relevant policy requirements including but not limited to London Plan Policy SI 13, its associated Sustainable Design and Construction SPG, the Non-Statutory Technical Standards for Sustainable Drainage Systems.
